A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3M-Progress zebrafish study. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing experiments and methods to be matched despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original embodied-agent simulations, behavioral comparisons and analyses aligning model activity with previously collected zebrafish recordings, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and model-data alignment results and adds diagnostic analyses, including module-specific alignment and baseline-agent latent dynamics.

M1.justification: The evaluated method retains the same recurrent PPO agent, frozen ethological world model, online world model and absolute deviation of model-memory mismatch from its moving average. Appendix C.3 discusses possible multiple-prior extensions as future generalizations, without reporting a change to the implemented agent.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same zebrafish recording source, head-free pretraining environment and head-fixed futility-induced passivity setting, including active and passive transitions. The foraging and virtual-rodent examples in v2 Appendix C.3 are hypothetical, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The behavioral and whole-brain alignment comparisons retain the same intrinsic drives and control models. However, v2 Appendix B/Figure 7 adds latent-dynamics comparisons for gamma-Progress, ICM, RND, Disagreement, Homeostatic, MaxEnt and Random agents; v1's corresponding PCA presentation covered only 3M-Progress.

E3.justification: Figure 4 changes from passive-transition results to averages over active and passive transitions. Module evaluation also changes: v1 Figure 7 includes LSTM blocks and decoder hidden layers, whereas v2 Figure 6 explicitly excludes module read-in/readout layers where applicable. The introductory cell-count estimate changes from approximately 300,000 to over 250,000, without establishing that different recordings were used.

E4.justification: v2 adds PCA traces for seven control agents, enabling assessment of whether the latent patterns shown for 3M-Progress are distinctive. Its module analysis also expands from passive transitions to both transition directions and separately displays neural/glial alignment, substantially broadening the mechanistic diagnostics.

E5.justification: Both versions already display error bars and noise-corrected alignment. v2 Appendix F newly documents split-half bootstrapping, mapping and internal consistency, Spearman-Brown correction and standard-error summaries, substantially expanding statistical reporting. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit statement that rollout results average eight evaluation seeds; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Numerous alignment results change substantially: active-transition RND alignment is roughly 0.90–0.96 in v1 Figure 6 but approximately 0.25 in v2 Figure 6A, while 3M-Progress remains near ceiling. v2 also adds transition-averaged results, active-transition module scores and control-agent PCA findings. Given the revised unit-selection description, these are revised reported results, not demonstrated same-setting performance losses.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds a formal non-convergence argument for prediction-error-driven exploration and explicit consistency/support assumptions for partitioning behavioral space through world-model divergence. Appendix F adds substantial noise-correction derivations for subject pairs, multiple subjects, RSA and pooled populations, going well beyond v1's brief mismatch argument.

C1.justification: v2 adds the broader novelty claim of the first autonomous embodied agent predicting brain data entirely through self-supervised intrinsic-goal optimization without behavioral or neural training data. It also strengthens criticism of existing exploration methods into a non-convergence claim, while retaining the original neural-glial modeling and zebrafish-alignment contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets replayed-feedback findings as evidence for an internal predictive model and adds substantive discussion of niche-seeking, niche-avoiding and multiple-niche exploration in Appendix C.3. These extend applicability and mechanism interpretation; the existing limitations concerning ecological realism and simplified cellular biology remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-access pointers for the agent implementation and brainmodel_utils, identifies the noise-correction function and returned statistic, specifies the torque range and extensively documents alignment calculations. Most architecture and training hyperparameters match v1 Appendix D, so these are substantial reproducibility disclosures rather than evidence of changed training.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially expanded and repositioned around autonomous intrinsic learning versus imitation and downstream-task optimization. v2 replaces the Dreamer discussion with Plan2Explore and adds coverage including NeuroMechFly, OpenWorm, musculoskeletal models, robotic zebrafish circuits, digital twins and predictive-learning research.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, related work and discussion are extensively rewritten. Method motivation becomes a dedicated first-principles section, baseline definitions move into reorganized appendices, and the introduction gains an explicit contribution list. The title, author information and publication header also change.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn for transition-averaged results, and earlier transition/module plots are reorganized into the four-panel Figure 6. v2 introduces a seven-panel baseline PCA Figure 7 and corrects Figure 2's agreement/disagreement labeling. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves auditability through added diagnostic comparisons, clearer organization and code/metric documentation. However, it removes the eight-seed disclosure and strengthens convergence claims using an Appendix C.1 argument that does not justify inferring zero reward for every policy from zero loss only on visited support. These substantive benefits and weaknesses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
